claims.text: The patient presented with severe left knee pain and functional limitation due to end-stage osteoarthritis, described as a constant dull ache with sharp pain on weight-bearing, rated 8/10 to 9/10, worsening over 12 months.
Past medical history was limited to end-stage osteoarthritis of the left knee, with no other significant conditions reported.
Family history included type 2 diabetes in the mother and hypertension in the father, with no family history of osteoarthritis or anaesthetic complications.

Social history indicated the patient lived with parents, was independent in activities of daily living but required assistance for prolonged walking or standing, was a non-smoker, drank approximately 4 units of alcohol per week, and had no recreational drug use.
No known drug or environmental allergies were reported across multiple assessments.

Pre-operative examination on 20/12/25 revealed significant left knee deformity with valgus alignment, medial joint line tenderness, reduced range of motion with pain beyond 70 degrees flexion, and mild effusion, with no signs of erythema, warmth, or infection.
Cardiovascular and respiratory examinations on 20/12/25 were normal, with normal heart sounds, no murmurs, no peripheral oedema, equal bilateral air entry, and no wheeze or crackles.
Vital signs on 20/12/25 were HR 72 bpm, BP 124/78 mmHg, RR 16 br/min, Temp 36.8°C, and SpO2 98%.
Investigations on 20/12/25 showed mild anaemia with Hb 11.3 g/dL, while WCC, platelets, U&E, LFT, CRP, urinalysis, and ECG were within normal limits.
Anaesthetic assessment on 20/12/25 assigned ASA grade I, with a Mallampati score of I, adequate mouth opening, normal neck mobility, and normal thyromental distance.
Ferrous sulfate 200 mg once daily was prescribed on 20/12/25 to address mild anaemia, with advice to increase dietary iron intake.
The patient was cleared for general anaesthesia on 20/12/25, with instructions for carbohydrate loading the day prior to surgery and fasting from midnight.
Formal written consent for total left knee replacement was obtained on 21/12/25, with risks including infection, thromboembolism, and neurovascular injury discussed.
Pre-operative assessment on 21/12/25 confirmed fitness for surgery, with vital signs HR 76 bpm, BP 120/7 mmHg, RR 16/min, SpO2 98%, and BMI 24.
The patient was admitted electively on 05/01/26 for total left knee replacement, with pre-operative checklist completed and fasting compliance confirmed.
Admission examination on 05/01/26 showed gross left knee deformity consistent with end-stage OA, no erythema or effusion, and normal cardiovascular and respiratory findings.
Admission observations on 05/01/26 were HR 74 bpm, BP 122/78 mmHg, RR 14 br/min, Temp 36.7°C, and SpO2 98% on room air.

Total left knee replacement was performed on 05/01/26 under general anaesthesia, with findings of severe cartilage degeneration and subchondral bone exposure, and implantation of a cemented total knee prosthesis.
Intra-operative management included administration of Cefuroxime 1.5g IV for prophylaxis, with minimal blood loss and no complications.
Post-operative care plan on 05/01/26 included Tinzaparin 4,500 units subcutaneously once daily for thromboprophylaxis and Paracetamol 1g orally QDS PRN for pain.
The patient was transferred to the PACU on 05/01/26, where a PCA pump with IV morphine 2 mg was initiated for pain management, and oxygen therapy at 2L/min via nasal cannula was provided.
Post-operative ward review on 05/01/26 reported moderate pain (6/10) with discomfort on movement, clean surgical site with minimal serous drainage, and no signs of infection or DVT.

Medication records conflict regarding thromboprophylaxis: note-7 and note-8 prescribe Tinzaparin 4,500 units SC once daily starting 05/01/26, while note-9 plans to start Enoxaparin 40 mg SC once daily on 05/01/26.
Pain management plan on 05/01/26 included Paracetamol 1g every 6 hours regularly and Codeine phosphate 30 mg PRN for breakthrough pain.
Physiotherapy on 06/01/26 focused on gentle mobilisation, achieving 40 degrees flexion with mild discomfort (VAS 4/10), and deep breathing exercises.
Observations on 06/01/26 during physiotherapy were HR 78 bpm, BP 122/78 mmHg, SpO2 98% on room air, with patent airway and no respiratory distress.
Ward round on 06/01/26 reported mild pain well controlled with oral analgesia, clean and dry surgical site, and no signs of DVT.
Observations on 06/01/26 were HR 78, BP 118/72, RR 16, Temp 36.8, and SpO2 98% on room air.
Plan on 06/01/26 included continuing Enoxaparin 40 mg SC OD for thromboprophylaxis until discharge and maintaining current pain management.
Physiotherapy on 07/01/26 involved walking with a Zimmer frame and assisted knee exercises, with mild discomfort (3/10) and no adverse events.
Observations on 07/01/26 during physiotherapy were BP 120/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16/min, SpO2 98% on room air, and GCS 15/15.
Pharmacist review on 07/01/26 recommended switching IV paracetamol to PO 1g QDS and continuing Ibuprofen 400mg TDS if tolerated.
Occupational therapy on 07/01/26 assessed ADLs, recommending home adjustments including a raised toilet seat and sock aid, with the patient maintaining good balance with verbal prompts.
Ward round on 07/01/26 reported manageable pain, improved mobility with physio, and mild post-operative anaemia with Hb 108 g/L.
Observations on 07/01/26 were HR 82, BP 125/78, RR 16, Temp 36.7, and SpO2 97% on room air.
Plan on 07/01/26 included prescribing Ferrous sulfate 200 mg BD for post-op anaemia and transitioning to oral Ibuprofen 400 mg TDS for pain management.
Ward round on 08/01/26 reported satisfactory pain control, effective mobilisation with Zimmer frame, and persistent mild anaemia with Hb 108 g/L.
Observations on 08/01/26 were HR 72, BP 118/76, RR 16, Temp 36.8, and SpO2 98% on room air.
Plan on 08/01/26 included switching regular paracetamol to PRN dosing, prescribing Co-amoxiclav 500/125 mg TDS for 7 days for wound infection prophylaxis, and continuing Ferrous sulfate 200 mg BD.
Final physiotherapy session on 08/01/26 focused on crutch use and stair navigation, with the patient deemed safe for discharge with crutches.
Observations on 08/01/26 during physiotherapy were BP 118/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, and SpO2 97% on room air.
Discharge planning on 08/01/26 included wound care instructions, pain management with oral Paracetamol 1g QDS and Ibuprofen 400mg TDS, and a follow-up appointment scheduled for 15/01/26.
Occupational therapy review on 08/01/26 confirmed independence in ADLs and readiness for discharge with crutches, with discharge planned for the following day.
